title: “The Authority You Forgot You Had”
paragraphs: “The Authority You Forgot You Had”
The Deeper Meaning of Luke 10:19 and Why So Many Believers Live Below What Christ Already Gave Them
There are moments in life when fear feels louder than faith.
The doctor's report arrives.
The marriage begins to crack.
The temptation returns.
The anxiety refuses to leave.
The memories you buried start speaking again in the middle of the night.
And somewhere between the pressure, the disappointment, and the spiritual battles nobody else can see, many Christians quietly begin believing a lie:
“I am powerless.”
It is one of Satan’s oldest strategies.
Not merely to tempt you.
Not merely to discourage you.
But to convince you that you have forgotten who Jesus is and what Jesus has already given to those who belong to Him.
That is why Luke 10:19 hits with such force.
Jesus says:
“Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.” (Luke 10:19, KJV)
In the original Greek text, Jesus says:
“Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ.”
A more literal rendering would be:
“Behold, I have given you the authority to walk upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy.”
The distinction matters.
Jesus did not merely say He gave His followers power.
The Greek word translated as “power” in the first part of the verse is exousia (ἐξουσία).
It means delegated authority.
Legal authority.
The right to act on behalf of another.
In the second part of the verse, the word translated as the enemy's power is dynamis (δύναμις), meaning strength, force, or ability.
This means Jesus is saying something extraordinary.
He is declaring that the believer has been given authority that stands above the enemy's strength.
The enemy may possess force.
But Christ possesses the throne.
The enemy may possess influence.
But Christ possesses all authority in heaven and on earth.
The enemy may threaten.
But Jesus reigns.
This is not a promise that Christians will never suffer.
The Bible itself disproves that misunderstanding.
The apostles were persecuted.
Some were imprisoned.
Many were martyred.
Jesus Himself was crucified.
Luke 10:19 is not a guarantee of a painless life.
It is a declaration that Satan does not have ultimate authority over those who belong to Christ.
The context is important.
Seventy-two disciples had just returned amazed because demons submitted to them in Jesus' name.
They were astonished by what they had witnessed.
But Jesus redirected their attention.
Immediately after Luke 10:19, He says:
“Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” (Luke 10:20)
Notice what Jesus does.
He moves their focus from power to salvation.
From authority to relationship.
From victory in ministry to eternal security.
The greatest miracle is not that demons obey.
The greatest miracle is that sinners are saved.
And that is where the beauty of the Gospel explodes into view.
Because before we ever had authority over darkness, darkness had authority over us.
Before Christ, we were not merely fighting sin.
We were slaves to it.
Before grace, we were spiritually bankrupt.
Before forgiveness, we stood guilty before a holy God.
Before the cross, our story was headed toward judgment.
That is the scandal.
Not merely what we did.
But who we became apart from God.
Broken.
Rebellious.
Lost.
And yet Jesus stepped into our story.
Not when we deserved rescue.
Not when we finally got our lives together.
Not when we became respectable.
Christ came while we were still sinners.
He took our shame.
He carried our guilt.
He bore our punishment.
The authority of Luke 10:19 only exists because of the sacrifice of Calvary.
There is no authority without the cross.
No victory without the empty tomb.
No triumph without the blood of Jesus.
Many people read Luke 10:19 and immediately think about spiritual warfare.
And rightly so.
But perhaps the deepest serpent most people face today is not visible.
It is the voice that whispers:
“You'll never change.”
“You've gone too far.”
“You're too damaged.”
“You're too addicted.”
“You've failed too many times.”
“You'll always be this person.”
That voice has destroyed dreams.
Ruined ministries.
Broken families.
And kept countless believers trapped in cycles of shame.
Yet the Gospel answers back.
The enemy says your failures define you.
Jesus says His grace defines you.
The enemy points to your worst chapter.
Jesus points to His finished work.
The enemy reminds you where you have been.
Jesus reminds you where He is taking you.
That is why our message has always been simple:
Because Jesus rewrites everything.
The authority Jesus gives is not permission for arrogance.
It is freedom from fear.
It is confidence rooted in Christ.
It is the ability to stand when hell tells you to fall.
It is the courage to keep believing when circumstances say quit.
It is the strength to keep praying when answers seem delayed.
It is the confidence that your King is still on the throne even when life feels out of control.
Perhaps today you are fighting battles nobody knows about.
Perhaps you smile publicly while suffering privately.
Perhaps your faith feels exhausted.
Perhaps you are one disappointment away from giving up.
Hear the words of Jesus again.
“Ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν…”
“Behold, I have given you authority.”
Not because you are strong.
Because He is.
Not because you are worthy.
Because He is.
Not because you earned it.
Because He purchased it.
And maybe that is exactly what your soul needed to remember today.
You are not fighting for victory.
In Christ, you fight from victory.
You are not abandoned.
You are not forgotten.
You are not beyond redemption.
Be honest.
This may have hit harder than you expected.
